title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC first actual vs later; universal vs particular corruption
pass_a_gloss: Placeus repeats the disparity: the first actual sin corrupted nature; later sins do not likewise. Universal corruption (aversion from the true last end / conversion to a false one) propagates naturally and yields only to regeneration; particular determinations to certain objects do not so propagate and can sometimes change without regeneration. GAR should not have supposed both share one reason.
pass_b_english: PLAC. I have already shown that the reason of the first actual sin and of those that follow is very unequal: that corrupted nature, these do not likewise; and also of universal corruption seated in aversion from the true last end and conversion to a falsely apparent last end, and of that particular determination of corruption to certain objects—for the former is naturally propagated, the latter not likewise; the former can be taken away only by regeneration, the latter can sometimes without regeneration be taken away or even changed into its opposite. Therefore the learned man ought not to have supposed that the reason of both is the same.
source_text: PLAC. Iam ostendi, valde disparem esse rationem primi peccati actualis, & sequentium; illud corrupisse naturam, ista non item; necnon corruptionis universalis in aversione a vero fine ultimo & conversione ad finem ultimum falso apparentem sitae, & corruptionis illius particularis determinationis ad certa quaedam objecta; illam enim naturaliter propagari, hanc non item; illam non nisi per regenerationem tolli posse, hanc posse nonnunquam absque regeneratione aut tolli, aut etiam in oppositam mutari. Non igitur virum doctum supponere decuit, eandem esse utriusque rationem.
